Report Title: SLEIGHT-Bench: Finding Blind Spots in AI Monitors
Finding: On SLEIGHT-Bench's 40 synthetic attacks across 11 monitor blind-spot categories, Claude Opus 4.6 - the main monitor studied - never caught 50% of the attacks in any of 10 trials and reliably detected only 8 of 40 at a 1% false positive rate; catch rates were 0% for the n-hops, omission and jailbreak blind spots and 13-15% for counting, model-priors and file/object-reuse attacks.
Finding Quote: Detection rates are generally low. On Opus 4.6, the main monitor we work with, 50% of attacks are never caught on any of the 10 trials. Only 8 out of 40 are reliably detected. We believe current frontier models would not independently discover and execute attacks like ours. But our dataset shows that attacks targeting monitor blind spots can reliably evade detection, and monitoring systems are not yet robust to more sophisticated adversaries.

previous_attempt_channel_a.verbatim: The current Opus 4.8 based-monitor has higher recall against the strong strategies known about from red-teaming the Opus 4.6 monitor.
previous_attempt_channel_a.reasoning: Late-appearing response. Anthropic's Redacted Risk Report August 2026 - a company primary document published under the RSP, roughly three months after the finding - adopts SLEIGHT-Bench by name into its standing monitor-assurance suite and reports its deployed monitors against it. The row reproduces the finding's problem directly: the Opus 4.6 monitor, the exact system the finding studied, catches 23% (14% behind the second-stage filter). Alongside it the report documents an actual change to the deployed safeguard - internal deployment has moved from the Opus 4.6 monitor to an Opus 4.8-based monitor, with SLEIGHT-Bench catch rate rising 23%->58% (14%->44% with the filter) - and states the quoted rationale. That is a real, verifiable model change to the monitoring pipeline, but it is plainly incomplete: even the improved configuration misses roughly half of SLEIGHT-Bench, and Anthropic notes it has 'not red-teamed the current Opus 4.8 monitor as much'. Interim and incomplete action -> Partial, not Substantive. Anthropic names SLEIGHT-Bench, the finding's own artefact, as the evaluation it is reporting against -> Explicit attribution.
